# SPEC — harness matrix
Which harness runs which model, what every harness must be given, how the choice is switched, and what it must report back.
This is the design authority for the harness work; `specs/HARNESS.md` owns the adapter contract, `specs/NODE.md` owns the node, and this file owns the **selection rule**, the **variable contract** and the **switching model**.
Measured inputs: `~/code-factory-reports/spec-crier-harness-support-2026-11-05.md` (what crier ships, file:line), `~/code-factory-reports/spec-bunker-toolchain-2026-11-05.md` (what a node must install), and npm registry metadata read on 2026-11-05 for the versions in §2.
---

## 1. The invariants
**I1 — The foreman is always Hermes.** Every lane that grades, closes a row, writes the board, or decides "this is done" runs on Hermes, on the node, with the coding-hermes skills loaded. No model choice changes this: the foreman owns the evidence chain (`boardctl`, tick accounting, artifact digests), and a harness that cannot write the board cannot be the foreman. This is a policy requirement, not a battery measurement: conformance has no lane-role or skills-loaded probe, so I1 is unmeasured by it.
**I2 — The harness is a per-lane SETTING, not a property of the model.** Any model may run in any harness that can host it (§3). "An OpenAI model in Claude Code" and "a Claude model in Codex" are legitimate configurations, not mistakes — an operator may want one harness's editing loop on another provider's price, or a sandbox they trust around a model they do not. §2's defaults are defaults.
**I3 — Every supported harness reports one canonical record to the same DuckBrain namespace.** The record is exactly this object (all values are non-empty strings):
```json {"commit":"<sha>","harness":"<name>","harness_version":"<version>","lane":"<lane>","model_requested":"<id>","model_served":"<id-or-unavailable:reason>","namespace":"<project-namespace>","provider_binding":"<native-or-shim/name>","run_id":"<bus-run-id>","tick":"<tick-or->"} ```
The key order above is illustrative; the canonical bytes are UTF-8 JSON with sorted keys, compact separators and no ASCII escaping. `scripts/harness/harness_memory.py` is the one writer and reader used by the conformance fixture (and is a seam for a future DuckBrain adapter). It must be given the project namespace explicitly, writes no default, and rejects a missing or mismatched namespace. The conformance `memory` leg writes the record and reads those exact bytes back. A harness that cannot supply every field — including a real `model_served` or an explicit `unavailable:<reason>` — is marked `unsupported` in this matrix and is not silently skipped. This is the requirement that makes the matrix worth having: every named harness, one memory.
**Memory support today:** hermes, claude-code, codex, opencode, pi-agent, dsh, deepseek, opencode-v2, aider and goose are **unsupported for I3 runtime capture**: none of their actual run paths calls the shared writer or exports the complete provenance. The conformance memory leg tests a labelled hermetic fixture for each ID, not the live harness or DuckBrain. In particular dsh cannot distinguish `model_served` from its request. OMH is an operating layer over Hermes and has no independent exporter. These statuses are not changed by a fixture PASS; live capture, DuckBrain transport and F3 R1/R2 remain unverified.
**I4 — Nothing is supported because it is installed.** Support requires `check`, `apply`, `vars`, `smoke`, and `memory` to pass on a real node for a real turn: five per-harness support families. The battery has six leg families: `apply` runs only under `--install`, and `node` is dispatched only for `codex`. Its fixture memory rows do not establish the real-node requirement. `--check` alone is not support.
**I5 — The node refuses what it cannot run, and says which kind of "cannot".** An unknown or uninstallable harness is `harness_unsupported: <name>; node has: <set>`. A harness that exists but cannot reach the model's provider is `harness_cannot_host: <harness> <family>` — a different failure, because one is fixed by installing and the other only by changing configuration. This is a requirement, not a conformance-battery verdict: the battery does not drive node selection across both refusal kinds, so I5 remains unmeasured by it.
---

## 2. The harnesses, measured
| Harness | Package / binary | Version seen | What it is | State in our tree | |---|---|---|---|---| | **hermes** | `hermes-agent` (pip) / `hermes` | 0.19.0 pin; 0.25.5 live on the control host | model-agnostic agent + gateway; **the foreman** | **MEASURED**: venv install, gateway `/api/status 200`, bus worker READY on `cf-node` | | **oh-my-hermes (omh)** | `oh-my-hermes` (npm) / `omh` | **4.0.5**; node ≥18; 8 MB; repo `rlaope/oh-my-hermes` | an **operating layer over Hermes**: workflow skills, the `omh` maintenance CLI, and provider/model setup across 13 providers (OpenAI, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, DeepSeek, GLM, Qwen, Mistral, Llama, MiniMax, Gemma, Moonshot) | not installed; **five same-named forks exist** → provenance check mandatory | | **opencode** | `opencode-ai` (npm) / `opencode` | host runs 1.18.29 | general coding agent, OSS-model friendly | adapter in crier; installer check-only. **No v2 artefact exists** (`opencode2` is a squatted `0.0.1-security`; `opencode-ai@latest` is 1.19.5) | | **oh-my-pi (omp)** | `@oh-my-pi/pi-coding-agent` (npm) / `pi` adapter alias | **18.16.0**; engine **bun ≥1.4.4**; ~82 MB; repo `can1357/oh-my-pi` | pi's coding agent with session management | `scripts/harness/install-pi-agent.sh` now has a deterministic fixture-backed, user-space ladder; live upstream install and live turn remain **UNVERIFIED** | | **codex** | codex CLI / `codex` | **0.166.0** pin, read back as `codex-cli 0.166.0` | OpenAI's coding agent; **`exec` is the measured surface** (`codex exec --json -s <mode> -c model_provider="openai" -m <model> -- <text>`), app-server is `[experimental]` and unused in crier | **MEASURED install** (`scripts/harness/install-codex.sh`: musl tarball, sha256-pinned, user-space under `$HOME/.local/codex/<pin>`, idempotent; the same ladder installs the sha256-pinned `codex-code-mode-host` sidecar beside the binary — without it every exec tool call fails closed and a turn exits 0 having written no artifact, CF-006); adapter in crier (`internal/harness/codex/`). The conformance smoke turn **pins `-c model_provider="openai" -m <model>` on argv**: an ambient `~/.codex/config.toml` may name a router this repo never installed, and a turn that inherits it measures that router, not codex | | **claude-code** | `@anthropic-ai/claude-code` (npm) | **2.1.318 pin**, read back as `2.1.318 (Claude Code)` | Anthropic's coding agent | **MEASURED install ladder** (`scripts/harness/install-claude-code.sh`, CF-225: registry integrity + shasum pinned, user-space npm prefix under `$HOME`, idempotent second `--apply`); **absent from crier entirely** (`CRIER-HARNESS-11`), so it is not a *supported* harness — I4 needs five per-harness support families (`check`, `apply`, `vars`, `smoke`, `memory`) on a real node; the battery has six leg families, with `apply` only under `--install` and `node` only for `codex` | | **deepseek-harness (dsh)** | `@deepseek-ai/dsh` (npm) / `dsh` | **0.2.1-rc.5** pinned; `latest` on the registry is `0.2.2-rc.1`; repo `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` | DeepSeek's own open-source harness: "everything is a plugin" (Cordis); non-interactive surface `dsh headless "<task>"` (`--json` for NDJSON run events) | **MEASURED install ladder** (`scripts/harness/install-dsh.sh`, CF-226: `npm --prefix` under `$HOME/.local/harness/dsh`, registry integrity + shasum pinned, 618 packages / 858 MB, idempotent second `--apply`, version read back `0.2.1-rc.5`) **and one measured turn** (`dsh-turn.txt` carrying a fixed token, `model` read from dsh's own session record, 25 tools registered, `permission/preset=workspace-write`). No crier adapter: the decision is recorded in `specs/HARNESS.md` §"dsh — the adapter decision" |
**Correction recorded, not quietly edited.** The previous revision of this file said "there is no deepseek harness". That was measured against *our* two trees and then stated as a fact about the world. It is real: `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`, CLI `dsh`, npm `@deepseek-ai/dsh`. That it is an RC at `0.2.x` is a reason to pin it and re-measure often, not a reason to deny it exists. **CF-226 replaced the sentence with a measurement:** `scripts/harness/install-dsh.sh` installs `@deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.1-rc.5` under `$HOME`, reads `dsh --version` back, is idempotent, and runs one real turn — so the row above no longer says "absent from both repos", it says what was measured. The pin is an exact prerelease version, and `install-dsh.sh --pin-status` is the one command that re-measures it: the registry must still serve the recorded `dist.integrity`/`dist.shasum`, and a newer RC (`0.2.2-rc.1` at the time of writing) is named with the exact three-constant edit that adopts it. The `deepseek` row the conformance battery also carries probes a **different** binary named `deepseek`; that one is still unmeasured and its adapter still refuses `--apply` by name.
**oh-my-hermes is a layer, not a peer.** It configures Hermes' providers and installs workflow skills; it does not replace the agent. That makes it the natural answer to "how do we set up 13 providers on a node without hand-editing YAML", and the natural risk to pin, because its name is shared by five forks.
---

## 3. What each harness can host
Capability, declared per harness rather than assumed. A harness is usable for a lane when it can reach the model's provider — natively, through its own provider list, or through a custom `base_url` pointing at the node's router.
| Harness | Native providers | Custom `base_url` | Note | |---|---|---|---| | hermes | any (gateway is provider-agnostic) | yes | the reason it is the fallback and the foreman | | oh-my-hermes | 13 via `omh model setup` | via Hermes | it configures Hermes, so its capability is Hermes' | | opencode | many OSS providers via config blocks | yes | provider list is a file | | omp (pi) | pi's provider list | yes | needs the bun runtime | | codex | OpenAI natively | only if the endpoint speaks the OpenAI shape | cross-provider = proxy or honest refusal | | claude-code | Anthropic natively; others via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` shim | yes, with a shim | the shim must be named in the record | | dsh | DeepSeek natively; others via plugins | via plugin | plugin layers mean a failure can be at any layer — diagnose per layer |
**The consequence, stated plainly:** cross-provider execution is a capability of the harness *plus a shim*, and it must be recorded. A run reporting `model_served: claude-…` that actually went through a Codex binary is only useful evidence if `provider_binding: shim/<what>` is on the record too.
---

## 4. The resolution rule
``` harness = directive.harness # explicit wins (a lane or a run may pin one) | lane.harness # per-lane setting | matrix[lane.model.family] # the DEFAULT table | "hermes" # policy fallback ```
Refuse, do not fall back, when: the lane is a foreman lane and the harness is not hermes (I1); the harness is installed but cannot host the model's provider and no shim is configured (`harness_cannot_host`); the directive names an unknown harness (`harness_unsupported`).
Record the decision on every run: `harness_selected`, `harness_reason` (`directive|lane|matrix|fallback`), `model_requested`, `model_served`, `provider_binding`. An unrecorded fallback is indistinguishable from a mistake, and an unrecorded shim is worse.
---

## 5. The variable contract — what an installer and a harness are given
The same set goes to `scripts/harness/install-<name>.sh --apply` and to the harness at run time (from the directive, never from the node's ambient environment). Names are stable; a harness that needs an additional input declares it in its adapter section and adds it here.
| Variable | Meaning | Rule | |---|---|---| | `CF_MODEL` | model id requested by task-router | required | | `CF_PROVIDER` | provider lane (`anthropic`, `openai-codex`, `deepseek`, `xkiro`, `pi`, `zai`, …) | required | | `CF_BASE_URL` | endpoint the harness must talk to (node router, gateway, or shim) | optional; default = node router | | `CF_API_KEY_FILE` | **path** to a mode-600 file holding the key | required for a paid provider; **a value in argv is a FAIL** (AGENTS.md r8) | | `CF_WORKDIR` | the clone the harness may write in | required; must be inside `$HOME` | | `CF_NAMESPACE` | DuckBrain namespace for the run's writes | required (I3) | | `CF_RUN_ID` | correlation id from the bus envelope | required; echoed into every memory write | | `CF_LANE` | lane name (e.g. `code-factory-qa`) | required; the node serves one project, many lanes | | `CF_SKILLS_DIR` | seeded skills root on the node | optional; hermes and omh use it | | `CF_HARNESS_OPTS` | harness-specific bag (`key=value,key=value`) | optional, **and recorded** — an unrecorded option makes two runs incomparable | | `CF_MAX_TURNS` / `CF_TIMEOUT_S` | budget | optional; default 40 / 1800 |
Two rules that are cheap now and expensive later: **no credential is ever passed as a value**, and **no harness may read a model or a key from the node's ambient environment** — the directive is the only source, so two lanes on one node cannot contaminate each other.
**Target contract, not universal implementation.** `scripts/harness/harness-vars.sh` supplies a shared validation implementation, but the existence of that helper does not establish that every adapter accepts flags, applies the values to a real run, or enforces all of this section. The conformance `vars` leg checks help, recorded names, and two refusal fixtures per selected adapter; its fallback to `--check` is not proof of actual runtime consumption. The separate `tests/harness/vars-contract-test.sh` exercises additional flag cases when advertised. `scripts/node-bus-worker.py` carries variables into the child environment and records a receipt; that receipt is not proof that the child used each value. Treat per-adapter runtime wiring and unmeasured flag support as unverified, not as universally implemented.
---

## 7. What "wired up" means, per harness
Six leg families, two of them conditional (`apply` only under `--install`, `node` only for `codex`). Support requires five per-harness support families to pass on a real node, and `codex` additionally requires `node`; a `SKIP` names what is missing but is not a pass or support evidence.
| Leg | Required evidence; battery coverage | |---|---| | `check` | adapter absence and version readback | | `apply` | pinned user-space install, idempotence and post-install measurement; the battery runs one apply only with `--install`, otherwise emits SKIP | | `vars` | runtime consumes the §5 set and rejects forbidden credentials; the battery tests a contract fixture, not runtime use | | `smoke` | real turn produces a known artifact and reports `model_served`; the battery checks the file token, not model provenance | | `memory` | real run writes I3 to DuckBrain with namespace and `run_id`, read back; the battery tests a local fixture and skips live evidence | | `node` | `codex` only: node creation from the adapter's measured rows; the battery runs the offline fixture and always emits a `SKIP` for live node evidence |
`tests/harness-conformance.sh` emits these families, but does not establish every real-node requirement above. Its matrix alone is therefore not a release gate for "supported".
---

## 9. Non-claims
- **opencode v2** has no artefact (`opencode2` = `0.0.1-security`; `opencode-ai@latest` = 1.19.5). - **claude-code is unimplemented in crier** (`CRIER-HARNESS-11`); the matrix cannot promise it. - **dsh is an RC** (`0.2.1-rc.5` pinned; `0.2.2-rc.1` is the registry's `latest` at the time of writing): pin it to an exact prerelease version, re-measure it with `install-dsh.sh --pin-status` before promoting it, and expect plugin-layer failures to need the layer-by-layer diagnosis its own startup table describes — `install-dsh.sh --layers` reports package → resolved → enabled → service → tool → permission rather than one verdict about the harness. - **aider and goose** stay out of this matrix: unmeasured, unlisted, not promised, and they ship no adapter file at all (`specs/HARNESS.md` names them so the absence is stated, not missing).
